svg.title: Cationic polymerisation mechanism of isobutylene
svg.desc: Initiation by a proton from BF3 and water, propagation by carbocation addition to monomer, and termination by chain transfer with loss of a proton, with full curved arrows.
svg.text: 1. Initiation: co-catalyst makes a strong acid; H+ attacks the π bond
2. Propagation: carbocation adds to the CH2 end of the next monomer (tertiary cation is stabilised)
3. Termination: chain transfer (β-H loss) regenerates the catalyst
Needs electron-releasing substituents (isobutylene, vinyl ethers, styrene); polar non-nucleophilic solvent; −80 to −100 °C.
